subject: Materials Science
title: The Immune Response to Implants
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Immune Response to Implants.

hook.text: Your body treats every implant as an invader — proteins coat its surface within seconds of insertion.

buildup.text: Protein adsorption is the first event — which proteins stick determines whether cells attack or accept the implant.

discovery.text: Macrophages arrive and try to engulf the foreign object — if they fail, they fuse into giant cells and wall it off.

twist.text: A fibrous capsule around an implant isn't failure — for some devices like pacemakers, encapsulation is expected.

climax.text: Understanding the foreign body response lets engineers design surfaces that guide healing instead of fighting it.

punchline.text: Every implant must pass the body's defense system — that's biocompatibility.

quiz.question: What is the first event when an implant enters the body?
options: Proteins adsorb onto its surface within seconds
The immune system ignores it completely
